hook_text: Thirty degrees north, thirty-one degrees east. Which city is hiding there?
clip_script: Bloemfontein, a treasure hunt on a wall map. On a flat map, lines of latitude run across and lines of longitude run up and down, making a grid. Clue one: thirty degrees north, thirty-one degrees east. Go up from the equator, then right from Greenwich: Cairo, in Egypt! Clue two: thirty degrees south, thirty-one degrees east: Durban! Same numbers, opposite sides of the equator. Latitude first, then longitude. Every place has an address in degrees.
visual_style: Whiteboard world map with a grid, a finger tracing up from the equator and across from Greenwich, landing on Cairo, then Durban.
mood: Exciting and puzzle-like, like cracking a secret code.
pacing: Quick clue, slow trace along the lines, a reveal, then a mirror-image second clue.
call_to_action: Watch the full lesson and write the degree address of your own city.
